sections.title: 1. Why Should You Study Civil Engineering in Ireland?
items: Civil Engineering in Ireland

Ireland is a great destination for students interested in designing, building and maintaining infrastructure. Civil Engineering applies technical knowledge and practical problem solving to meet the needs of roads, bridges, buildings, water systems and sustainable development of cities.
Main benefits of studying Civil Engineering in Ireland:
Practical learning: learn through design projects, laboratories, fieldwork and engineering assignments.
Infrastructure Opportunities: Find careers in construction, transportation, water management, structural design, and infrastructure development.
Sustainability focus: Study energy-efficient buildings, resilient infrastructure and environmentally responsible construction.
Professional development: Accredited engineering programs may facilitate progression to professional engineering qualifications.
Further education: Proceed to specialized master's degree programmes in structural engineering, transportation, geotechnical engineering or construction management.
Compare universities based on course content, accreditation, industry placements, tuition fees and what type of civil engineering work you want to do.
Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance can help students explore these opportunities and understand the requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: 2. Civil Engineering Courses in Ireland
items: Irish universities offer undergraduate and postgraduate programs in Civil Engineering and related specializations.
Undergraduate courses
Bachelor of Engineering (BEng): A way to enter into engineering study, duration varies by qualification.
Bachelor of Engineering (Honours): Usually a 4-year program.
Integrated Master of Engineering (MEng): A five-year program combining undergraduate and graduate level engineering.
- Civil Engineering - Structural Engineering
- Geotechnical Engineering
- Transportation Engineering
Trending topics
- Engineering math and mechanics.
- Structural design and analysis
- Building materials
- Geotechnical engineering and geotechnics
- Fluid mechanics and hydraulic
- Transportation and highway engineering
- Surveying and measuring land
- Project management and construction planning
- Engineer for the environment
- Structural modeling and computer aided design

sections.title: 3. Best Universities and Institutions for Civil Engineering in Ireland
4. Qualification to Study Civil Engineering in Ireland
items: Eligibility varies with the institution, qualification level and the educational background of the applicant.
Eligibility for Undergraduates
Students applying after Class 12 are usually required to:
A recognized secondary school qualification.
Mathematics with excellent academic performance.
Physics or other science subjects as required.
Grades that meet the entry requirements of the university.
Proof of English proficiency, if applicable.
Indian students should look at how their class 12 board, marks and subject combination is treated. Some applicants may need a foundation programme or other recognized qualification.

sections.title: 5. Civil Engineering Eligibility Criteria in Ireland
items: International students should look at the admission requirements for each programme separately.
University requirements
Universities evaluate academic grades, subject requirements and qualification equivalence.
Mathematics is particularly important and Physics may be required for entry to an undergraduate course.
English language requirements
Applicants may be required to provide results from IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or another recognized English language proficiency test.
Scores required vary between institutions and programs.
Certain universities may accept alternative proof of English competency.
Further requirements
Applicants may be required to:
Depending on the course
Certificates
Academic transcripts
Personal statement or statement of purpose
Recommendation letters
CV or resume for postgraduate application
Proof of relevant work experience if requested
Confirmation of application fee if applicable

sections.title: 6. Cost of Studying Civil Engineering in Ireland
items: Tuition costs for Civil Engineering in Ireland differ based on the institution, the specific program, the academic year, and the applicant's fee classification.
Published examples for international or non-EU undergraduate applicants for the academic year 2026/27 include
University of Galway | Civil Engineering | €27,640 inclusive of listed levy
University College Cork | Civil, Structural and Environmental Engineering | €27,000 + €210 capitation
Cost of living
Plus, plan for costs beyond tuition
Housing and communal services
Groceries and food
Transport public
Laptop, Books and study materials
Healthcare insurance
Immigration and registration fees, if applicable
Personal spending and emergency savings
The cost of living in Ireland will depend on the city and accommodation arrangements.

sections.title: 7. How to Get Into Civil Engineering in Ireland
8. Accreditation and Recognition of Civil Engineering in Ireland
items: Accreditation is an important factor when choosing an engineering degree.

Engineers Ireland accredits engineering programs against recognized educational and professional standards. Subject to the relevant requirements, an accredited program can be a basis for continuing professional development and for progression to professional engineering status.

Accreditation does not automatically mean employment, professional registration or recognition in every country. If you intend to work in India or elsewhere after graduation, check the relevant professional and qualification recognition requirements.

sections.title: 9. Salary and Job Opportunity for Civil Engineers in Ireland
items: Graduates of Civil Engineering in Ireland can get jobs in construction, infrastructure development, engineering consultancy, environmental services and project delivery
Typical career paths
- Engineer Civil Structural Engineering
- Engineer, Site
- Geotechnical Engineering
- Engineer, Transportation
- Environmental and Water Engineer
- Engineer - Construction Project
- Quantity Surveying / Cost-Engineering related functions, with suitable further training
- Engineer, Infrastructure Designing
- Project Manager
Further training, relevant experience or additional professional qualifications are required for some posts.
Salary expectations in Ireland
The figures below are indicative planning estimates of annual gross salaries and are not official salary scales or guarantee offers

Early career engineer | €40,000–€55,000
Experienced engineer | €55,000–€75,000+

faqs.q: Q1. How long is a civil engineering degree in Ireland?
faqs.a: Many undergraduate honors engineering degrees are four years long. Some integrated Master of Engineering courses are five years in duration, but this varies depending on the university and the structure of the course.

faqs.q: Q2. What are the eligibility criteria for Indian students?
faqs.a: As a rule candidates should have a recognised Class 12 qualification with good Mathematics results and Physics or other science subjects where these are required. Each university has its own grade and subject requirements.

faqs.q: Q3. What is the cost of Civil Engineering for international students?
faqs.a: For 2026/27The University of Galway lists €27,640 per year including its levy while UCC lists €27,000 per year plus a €210 capitation fee for the specified engineering program. Additional living expenses apply and fees may vary.

faqs.q: Q4. Is Civil Engineering accredited in Ireland?
faqs.a: Some Irish engineering programs are accredited by Engineers Ireland. Don’t assume all programs are the same – check the exact course and qualification.

faqs.q: Q5. What type of jobs can I get after studying Civil Engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: Graduates may apply for jobs in civil and structural design, construction, transportation, geo-technical engineering, water management and infrastructure projects. Career outcomes depend on skills, experience, availability of vacancies and employment eligibility.
